text:
alex_g: quick sanity check — i'm about to push a terraform change for the EKS GPU pool. goal: add a small reserved capacity for critical inference jobs + keep spot for burst. putting launch_template with capacity reservation + mixed instances. can someone scan for obvious mistakes before i open the PR?

maria_dev: 👍 can you paste the snippet you're planning to apply?

alex_g: sure — planned tf block (rough):

```
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_lt" {
  name_prefix = "redwood-gpu-" 
  # AMI, user_data, etc.

  capacity_reservation_specification {
    capacity_reservation_preference = "open"
  }

  instance_market_options {
    market_type = "spot"
  }
}

resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu_nodes" {
  cluster_name    = aws_eks_cluster.main.name
  node_group_name = "gpu-pool"
  node_role_arn   = aws_iam_role.gpu_node.arn

  scaling_config { desired_size = 4; min_size = 1; max_size = 8 }
  launch_template { id = aws_launch_template.gpu_lt.id; version = "$Latest" }

  # labels/taints set via bootstrap args
}
```

maria_dev: looks mostly okay. couple of notes:
- capacity_reservation_specification on LT just sets preference; you need to create an actual capacity reservation (aws_ec2_capacity_reservation) and reference its id in the run_instances/launch template override if you want guaranteed slots. otherwise "open" just opts in.
- for mixed spot/on-demand, consider using mixed_instances_policy in an ASG or set overrides in launch template + managed nodegroup may not expose full mixed policy. the EKS managed node group has limitations.

alex_g: ack — i was hoping to avoid ASG+eksctl since we standardize on managed nodegroups, but maybe for this use-case we need a separate ASG-backed pool.

tj_ops: we should also think about taints/tolerations and kubelet capacity reporting. if you reserve capacity for critical jobs, those nodes should be tainted so only the inference daemonset or pods with tolerations land there. example taint: `nvidia.com/gpu=reserved:NoSchedule`.

sophia_infra: +1. also wiring for GPU driver DaemonSet secret — make sure the nodebootstrap user-data can access the SSM parameter or S3 URL. we had an incident where kubelet couldn't pull the driver because the node IAM didn't include s3:GetObject for the driver bucket.

alex_g: good catch. current LT user_data references `s3://redwood-gpu-drivers/${ami_version}.tgz` and we pass an instance profile `gpu-node-profile`. i'll add the s3 permissions in the tf role.

maria_dev: for the capacity reservation, suggestion: create a small aws_ec2_capacity_reservation in the preferred AZ(s), then in launch_template override you can set `CapacityReservationSpecification` with the reservation id. if rollout across AZs, you might want multiple small reservations.

alex_g: do we want the reservation to be zonal or regional? thinking zonal to minimize cross-AZ latency for NVLink workloads.

tj_ops: zonal is fine but cost increases. maybe reserve for a subset of AZs and rely on spot fallback in others. also add a node-label like `pool=reserved-gpu` and adjust k8s scheduler (PodAffinity) for the critical services.

sophia_infra: don't forget GPU quotas in the account — if we create capacity reservations we might hit limits for vGPU/GPU counts in certain AZs. i'll run a quick quota check and post results.

k8s-bot: quick note — existing `gpu-pool` has label `k8s.io/role=gpu` and taint `nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule`. current daemonset tolerations allow `nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule`.

maria_dev: for the TF PR, include a changelog comment describing: why reserved capacity, AZ choices, IAM changes (s3 permissions), and how to revert. that'll speed reviews.

alex_g: will do. i'll open the PR in a bit. pinging @maria_dev @tj_ops for reviews when it's up. thanks all :heart: 

tj_ops: quick ask — can you add a snippet for the k8s toleration/selector you'll use? helps reviewers.

alex_g: adding example node label + toleration for the PR: 

```
# node bootstrap adds label: pool=reserved-gpu
# pod spec snippet
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  nodeSelector:
    pool: reserved-gpu
```

maria_dev: perfect. i'll review once it's posted.

sophia_infra: i'll post quota check in ~15m. if anything blocks, i'll DM.

alex_g: thanks — i'll proceed with a draft PR and link here.
